protocol.name: eclipse_glass_v1
protocol.copyright: Copyright EclipseOS contributors. Apache-2.0 (F-05 section 3, 4): clients and toolkit bridges link the client side under any licence.
protocol.description:
A client asks the compositor to draw its glass material (blurred, bent, smoked backdrop with a lit hairline and seam, the same program a window bezel uses) under parts of one of its own surfaces: a taskbar chip, a widget, a launcher row. Each part is a pane, a rounded box with a tone. The client draws only the pane's content and leaves the pane's ground to the compositor.
The compositor only reads backdrop pixels into its own composition; the client never receives them. Panes restrict nothing and grant nothing.

interface.name: eclipse_glass_manager_v1
interface.description: The global. It sends `capability` on bind and again whenever the compositor starts or stops drawing glass panes (for example a change of decoration.blur.mode). While the capability is 0 the compositor draws no panes, and a client should draw its own ground.

entry.name: glass_exists
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a glass object

entry.name: bad_pane
entry.summary: a malformed panes array, an unknown tone, or a negative size

entry.name: too_many_panes
entry.summary: more than 64 panes in one set_panes

event.name: capability
event.description: 1 while the compositor draws glass panes, 0 while it does not.

request.name: get_glass
request.description: One per wl_surface; a second call while the first object lives is protocol error glass_exists.

interface.name: eclipse_glass_surface_v1

description.summary: the glass panes of one wl_surface

interface.description: The pane list is double-buffered surface state: `set_panes` writes the pending list and the next wl_surface.commit makes it current, together with the buffer it was drawn for, so a pane that moves or resizes with its content never lags it by a frame. A new object starts with no panes.

entry.name: focused
entry.summary: the focused cell: the same glass a step clearer

entry.name: away
entry.summary: a put-away cell: a ghost rim only

entry.name: latent
entry.summary: nothing at rest; lifts like plain when hovered

enum.name: state
enum.description: Bits OR-ed into a pane record's state field.

entry.name: hovered
entry.summary: the pointer is over the pane

request.name: set_panes
request.description:
`panes` is a packed array of pane records, each nine native-endian 32-bit fields:
int x, int y, int width, int height the box, surface-local logical pixels; clipped to the surface uint radius corner radius, logical pixels; capped at half the box's shorter side uint bezel width of the lit band inside the edge, logical pixels; 0 is the compositor's default uint tone a value of the tone enum uint state a bitfield of the state enum uint alpha 0..255, the pane's ground opacity, for a pane that is arriving or leaving
At most 64 panes (too_many_panes). A length that is not a multiple of 36 bytes, an unknown tone, or a negative size is bad_pane. Panes are drawn in array order; an empty array removes every pane.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface's panes are removed on its next commit.
